title: A Radio Segment on Bilal's Voice
script: Radio Host: [thoughtful] Good evening, listeners. Tonight we're exploring Bilal ibn Rabah's story with a caller who researches early Islamic history. Welcome to the show.
Caller: Thank you for having me. Bilal's endurance is honestly one of the most sobering accounts from that entire period.
Radio Host: [carefully] For listeners unfamiliar, can you summarize what he actually endured before his eventual freedom?
Caller: Certainly. As an enslaved man whose owner despised his newfound faith, he was dragged into the desert heat, a heavy stone pressed onto his chest.
Radio Host: [reflective] That sounds unbearable. Was he offered any way to end that suffering?
Caller: Repeatedly. His tormentors demanded he renounce his belief and invoke their idols instead, promising immediate relief if he simply complied.
Radio Host: [honestly] And he refused, even under something that extreme?
Caller: Every time. He reportedly kept repeating a single word affirming God's oneness, as though the torment couldn't reach whatever conviction anchored him.
Radio Host: [gently] What eventually changed his circumstances?
Caller: Abu Bakr negotiated his purchase and immediately freed him, an act that cost considerable wealth but apparently mattered little to him by comparison.
Radio Host: [calmly] I understand Bilal later became known for something beyond his suffering entirely.
Caller: Yes, his voice. He was chosen to deliver the call to prayer, becoming essentially the first person to perform that role publicly in Islam.
Radio Host: [encouraging] There's something poetic about a formerly enslaved man's voice becoming the sound that summoned an entire growing community.
Caller: Exactly, and after the Prophet's death, Bilal reportedly found it too painful to continue delivering that call, since it evoked memories almost unbearably vivid.
Radio Host: [seriously] That detail humanizes him considerably, showing grief alongside the resilience everyone usually emphasizes.
Caller: Precisely. Endurance and heartbreak coexisted in him, which is what makes his story feel genuinely complete rather than merely inspirational.

quiz.question: What did Bilal's owner do to punish him for his faith?
options: He imprisoned him indoors
He exiled him from the city
He dragged him into the desert heat with a heavy stone on his chest
He confiscated his belongings
quiz.explanation: He was dragged into the desert heat, with a heavy stone pressed onto his chest, because his owner despised his faith.

quiz.question: What did his tormentors repeatedly demand?
options: That he pay a fine
That he leave the city
That he renounce his belief and invoke their idols
That he work harder
quiz.explanation: His tormentors repeatedly demanded he renounce his belief and invoke their idols instead, promising relief if he complied.

quiz.question: What did Bilal reportedly keep repeating during the torment?
options: A plea for mercy
A single word affirming God's oneness
The names of his tormentors
A promise to comply
quiz.explanation: He reportedly kept repeating a single word affirming God's oneness throughout the torment.

quiz.question: How did Bilal gain his freedom?
options: He escaped on his own
Abu Bakr negotiated his purchase and immediately freed him
His owner released him voluntarily
He was traded for goods
quiz.explanation: Abu Bakr negotiated his purchase and immediately freed him, at considerable personal cost.

quiz.question: Why did Bilal find it painful to continue the call to prayer after the Prophet's death?
options: He lost his voice permanently
He was forbidden from continuing
He moved to another city
It evoked memories almost unbearably vivid
quiz.explanation: He reportedly found it too painful to continue, since delivering the call evoked memories almost unbearably vivid.
